The Center of the Location-Scale Rule

Source: R/expected_loc_scale.R
loc_scale_center.Rd

Returns, for each distinct shape, the standardized point at which loc_scale_expected() centers its rule, the point where the nodes cluster. It is zero except for the centered skew normal, whose density has its step at \(w = -r\) with \(r = \{2|\gamma_1|/(4-\pi)\}^{1/3}\, \mathrm{sign}(\gamma_1)\); at a skewness near the ceiling the step is too sharp for nodes clustered at zero. The compiled diagonal of that family uses the same center.

Usage

loc_scale_center(distrib, U)

Arguments

distrib

A distribution object.

U

The matrix of distinct shapes, one row per shape.

Value

A numeric vector with one entry per row of U.
